title: Shipyard and telecom workers
author: Editorial Desk
summary: The All India Shipyard Employees Federation and the Indian Telecom Employees Federation.
body:
Two smaller BMS federations deserve attention: the **All India Shipyard Employees Federation** and the **Indian Telecom Employees Federation**.

## Shipyards

India's shipyards, public and private, build naval vessels, commercial ships and offshore structures. The industry supplies a strategic capability and a large number of skilled jobs in welders, fitters, electricians and engineers. Issues include **contract workers' wages**, **safety in hull work and confined spaces**, and the wage structures in defence shipyards.

## Telecom

Telecom employees have seen enormous change: from the Department of Telecom to BSNL and MTNL, then the entry of private operators. Concerns include the **revival of BSNL**, **pensions**, **voluntary retirement** and the position of contract workers who maintain towers and cables.

## Why they matter

Shipbuilding is key to maritime strength, and telecom is the nervous system of the digital economy. Both need skilled people.

## BMS's contribution

BMS's usual role is to bring such sectors into one national table, so that their issues can be placed before the labour and sector ministries in the same way as those of large industries.
